target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosures D003 and D050 are both part of NOTE 1 (The Company) and describe the company's identity, product portfolio, and IP licensing policy. These map directly to the split 2024 NOTE 1 disclosures: D001 (Company identity), D002 (Product portfolio), and D003 (IP licensing). Each 2024 disclosure has specific corresponding evidence in the original 2023 text or shares the same specific subject matter within the same section.

previous_disclosures.summary: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. is a global semiconductor company that manufactures a wide range of products including CPUs, GPUs, APUs, chipsets, data center and professional GPUs, embedded processors, SoCs, DPUs, FPGAs, SOMs, SmartNICs, AI Accelerators, and Adaptive SoC products, and may occasionally sell or license intellectual property.
The Company may from time to time sell or license portions of its IP portfolio.

materiality_analysis.reason: The change involves restructuring the presentation of the company's product portfolio and IP licensing. The 2023 text listed products including 'AI Accelerators'. The 2024 text explicitly spells out 'Artificial Intelligence (AI) Accelerators' instead of the acronym 'AI Accelerators' in the list. The list of products remains effectively the same (no new product categories added or removed that would change the business model description). The IP licensing policy remains unchanged ('may sell or license'). This is a stylistic/terminological clarification without substantive business change.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Stylistic expansion of AI product terminology

materiality_analysis.reason: The product listing underwent a substantive change. The 2025 disclosure replaced 'x86 microprocessors' with the broader 'microprocessors' and replaced 'SmartNICs' (Smart Network Interface Cards) with 'AI NICs'. This reflects a shift in product categorization and branding, potentially indicating a strategic prioritization of AI-specific networking hardware over general-purpose networking, which changes the substance of the disclosed product portfolio.

peer_results.rationale: Provided candidates discuss general competitive risks and past IP litigation charges, which are not substantively comparable to the target's forward-looking disclosure on the strategic licensing and sale of its own IP portfolio.

Provided candidates detail a specific resolved litigation case and construction commitments, neither of which addresses the strategic licensing or sale of intellectual property assets as described in the target disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: General industry patent risk and claims overview
comparisons.peer_summary: As is typical in the semiconductor industry, others have asserted and may assert that Micron's products or manufacturing processes infringe their intellectual property rights, with specific claims detailed in the filing.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron disclose general industry practices regarding intellectual property, but their focus differs significantly: AMD describes its strategic capability to sell or license its own IP portfolio, whereas Micron highlights the external risk of third parties asserting infringement claims against its products. AMD's disclosure is proactive and asset-focused, while Micron's is defensive and risk-focused.

sentences.text: From time to time, the Company may also sell or license portions of its intellectual property (IP) portfolio.

As is typical in the semiconductor and other high-tech industries, from time to time, others have asserted, and may in the future assert, that our products or manufacturing processes infringe upon their intellectual property rights.

peer_results.rationale: Provided candidates focus on indemnification liabilities for IP matters and general litigation exposure, which are distinct from the target's specific disclosure regarding the potential sale or license of its IP portfolio.
